assessment.nobel_worthiness: Strongest case for a voice recognizable nowhere else. Densely patterned, visionary prose (Blinding; Solenoid) turns memory, the body and dream into a metaphysical project with sustained formal ambition. It has a clear imaginative and intellectual depth, and the poetry-to-prose range suggests a coherent whole-career achievement.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would centre on visionary, encyclopedic prose that fuses the lyric, the bodily and the cosmological, written in Romanian, with poetry and fiction as the main genres.
assessment.maturity: Decades of work with a consistent, evolving project, so the oeuvre appears durable and mature. Timing is not a constraint on the literary case.
uncertainties: Much of the effect depends on Romanian sentence rhythm and density, which I can only judge through translation.
I have not independently verified the full corpus; coverage of the poetry and early work in translation is partial.
Risk that length and elaboration shade into repetition in some volumes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: An uncompromising, original fictional method. Dreamlike worlds destabilize psychology, space and causality (Frontier; Love in the New Millennium) in a way that is hard to confuse with any other writer. The formal radicalism is sustained rather than occasional.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would concern an experimental, anti-realist prose that reimagines the inner life, written in Chinese.
assessment.maturity: A long career with a stable, deepening aesthetic. The achievement looks consistent across decades, though I cannot assess every volume.
uncertainties: Translation is a major filter: the strangeness of the prose may be partly a translation effect, and I cannot judge it in the original.
Uncertain how far the later work develops beyond the early method rather than repeating it.
The scope of the translated corpus is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Compressed, highly wrought French prose that turns obscure lives and the history of art into narrative inquiry (Small Lives; The Eleven). Language and form are the achievement; the voice is distinctive and exacting.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would address concentrated, sentence-level prose that re-imagines lost or minor lives and artistic vocation, written in French.
assessment.maturity: A small but concentrated body of work whose quality appears sustained. The modest volume raises a question about breadth against intensity.
uncertainties: The small oeuvre may be too narrow for some readers' standard of breadth.
English translations convey the style only partially, and the style is the core of the case.
I cannot confirm the full extent of the later writing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A sustained novelistic oeuvre that interrogates colonial memory, gender and the changing Portuguese society (The Murmuring Coast; The Wind Whistling in the Cranes) with formal care. It combines historical and psychological depth and a socially assigned-roles perspective with distinctive narration.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would address fiction that joins the intimate to colonial and national history, written in Portuguese.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of work with consistent quality. Timing is not pressing, and the oeuvre should hold up to a full-oeuvre reading.
uncertainties: Degree of stylistic singularity versus excellent but more conventional historical fiction is hard to judge in translation.
Not all of the oeuvre is available in languages I can read.
Her international profile may understate or overstate her standing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Encyclopedic, linguistically inventive fiction (Gravity's Rainbow; Mason & Dixon) that links systems of power, science and countercultural imagination. Few writers match its formal ambition and stylistic range, and the influence on later fiction is considerable.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would address encyclopedic, systems-minded fiction with comic and paranoid registers, written in English.
assessment.maturity: Long career with several major works. Later novels are less consistently regarded, so the sustained-quality question is open.
uncertainties: Unevenness in some later work is a legitimate concern.
The intellectual-ideal dimension in Nobel's will is arguable for an ironic, paranoid vision.
Fame and cultural stature are not themselves evidence of merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A radically inward fiction that builds its own system of landscape, memory and mental images (The Plains; Border Districts). The voice is unmistakable, with a rigorous, self-questioning syntax.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would address an introspective fiction of memory and imagined landscapes, written in English.
assessment.maturity: A long, consistent project with a distinctive late period. The narrow thematic range may be read as either rigor or limitation.
uncertainties: Narrowness of subject matter against significance across the body of work.
I have limited ability to verify the extent of the later books.
Reception outside a specialist readership is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large, polyphonic novels (Carpentaria; The Swan Book) remake the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time. The formal ambition and a voice rooted in a particular community's narrative tradition are strong.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would address polyphonic fiction that fuses Indigenous oral and political narrative with an expansive novelistic form, written in English.
assessment.maturity: Fewer major novels than some rivals; the body of work is still developing. This bears on the sustained-quality criterion.
uncertainties: Size of the oeuvre is relatively limited for a whole-life judgment.
Political and cultural significance must be kept separate from literary merit.
The nonfiction is outside what I can assess closely.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Uncanny narrative voices expose exclusion, family power and unstable belonging (Three Strong Women; My Heart Hemmed In). The control of tone and the way estrangement is built into the syntax is distinctive, and the drama adds range.
assessment.attribution: Single named writer. A citation would address uncanny, precisely controlled prose and theatre on exclusion and belonging, written in French.
assessment.maturity: Substantial body of work across decades with consistent quality. Exact assessment of the drama is limited.
uncertainties: I rely on translation for most of the work and can judge the French only indirectly.
Whether the oeuvre has the full depth of the strongest candidates is unclear.
The theatre is less accessible to me than the fiction.
